claims.text: The starting material is an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy produced by conventional casting.
The starting material has a uniform, fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
Y and Hf will be co-added at minor, controlled concentrations during casting.
Minor Y/Hf co-doping can leave the eutectic microstructure and phase constitution essentially unchanged.
Y/Hf additions promote stable, finely dispersed oxide or intermetallic particles at or near phase boundaries.
The proposed particles retard grain-boundary diffusion and microstructural coarsening.
Y/Hf co-doping refines the microstructure and stabilizes the lamellar phase interfaces.
Y/Hf co-doping reduces grain-boundary mobility and thereby inhibits diffusion-based room-temperature creep.
Y/Hf facilitates protective oxide-scale formation that improves corrosion resistance.
Y/Hf co-doping improves the high-temperature microstructural stability of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Y/Hf co-doping improves the room-temperature creep resistance of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Y/Hf co-doping improves the corrosion resistance of AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The doped alloy will have a lower room-temperature creep rate than undoped AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The doped alloy will undergo less degradation during extreme-temperature cycling than the undoped alloy.
The doped alloy will sustain less corrosion damage than the undoped alloy in aggressive salt environments.
Y/Hf co-doping will maintain or slightly improve both tensile strength and ductility.
The intervention is effective only at sufficiently low Y/Hf levels that do not disrupt the eutectic lamellar microstructure.
The optimum Y and Hf concentrations and the quantitative long-term improvements remain undetermined.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts reduced corrosion damage and reduced spallation, but the cited record reports a larger hot-corrosion spallation area for YHf-EHEA than for undoped EHEA (14.98% versus 5.67%). The record's concluding statement that co-doping improved oxide-scale spallation resistance is itself inconsistent with those reported values.
